_comment: Generated by parity/native/gen (cargo run, see the Makefile target native-goldens) from parity/native/mcp_cases.json; do not edit by hand. Each case is a /mcp workbench tool call: `native` lists the pflow-native commands it stands for, `expect` (or `error`) is what they return, in the tool's shape. Replayed by cmd/webserver/mcp_workbench_parity_test.go.

cases.name: pflow_sde/gated-refuses
cases.error: sde refused: this model constrains firing in ways continuous diffusion cannot express, so the SDE would silently model an unconstrained system. Use the discrete engine (Simulate). Specifically: 1 inhibitor arc(s) block a firing above a threshold; a continuous solver cannot test them; capacity is declared on [Queue Done] but is a post-firing bound, which has no continuous analogue

cases.name: pflow_sde/coffee-colored-refuses
cases.error: sde refused: this model constrains firing in ways continuous diffusion cannot express, so the SDE would silently model an unconstrained system. Use the discrete engine (Simulate). Specifically: capacity is declared on [WaitingCustomers.red CoffeeBeans.brown ServedCoffee.red] but is a post-firing bound, which has no continuous analogue

cases.name: pflow_sde/bad-dt
cases.error: dt must be a positive number

cases.name: pflow_sde/dt-over-cap
cases.error: dt 0.00001 needs 50000 sample intervals over t_end 10, over the 50000 cap; use a larger dt

scenarios.name: as is
assumptions: this engine assumes every step takes a random, exponentially distributed amount of time, which is the most erratic a shop can be for a given average. Work with a predictable duration — a shot pulls in about the same time every time — queues roughly half as much, so treat the waiting and the walkouts here as the bad case, not the typical one.

cases.name: pflow_optimize/sir-two-objectives-log
cases.why: log sampling: 10^x and log10 come from each language's math library and can differ in the last bit (measured: rates within 6e-16), and the ODE carries that to the objectives (measured: within 3e-13). Linearly sampled rates are still compared exactly

cases.name: pflow_optimize/gated-capacity-ignored
cases.why: log sampling: 10^x and log10 come from each language's math library and can differ in the last bit (measured: rates within 6e-16), and the ODE carries that to the objectives (measured: within 3e-13). Linearly sampled rates are still compared exactly

cases.name: pflow_optimize/coffee-colored
cases.why: the step controller's x^(1/6) comes from each language's math library (Go's math.Pow, glibc's pow under Rust), which can differ in the last bit and move a step (measured: objectives within 9e-16; the sampled rates are exact). RestockBeans is sampled in a non-stiff range: at the fixture's 720 the finals are limited by the solver tolerance and the two solvers' step sequences part (see parity/native/README.md)
